text:
marta: Heads-up — noticed sporadic 502s on canary for inference-gateway when we flipped the service to NodePort + NLB passthrough this morning. quick dump below, can someone sanity-check probe/targetPort mapping?

samir: ugh yes saw one alert. likely probe hitting the wrong port on node vs pod. which PR changed ports?

marta: PR #3456 — terraform change to k8s_service ports section. changed `port` from 8080 -> 443 for TLS passthrough and kept `targetPort: 8080`. not sure if that breaks nodeport probe routing.

leo: trying to recall: NLB health checks for nodeport mode hit the node IP on the nodePort, and the kube-proxy NATs it to pod targetPort. If nodePort != service.port mapping gets weird for named ports.

irene: can you paste the service manifest and the TF snippet? small diff helps.

marta: sure — service (generated by TF):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-gateway
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: tcp
spec:
  type: NodePort
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8080
      nodePort: 32080
  selector:
    app: inference-gateway
```
and the terraform change was: `port = 443` (was 8080) but `target_port = 8080` unchanged.

samir: that looks like you're telling the lb to check TCP:443 on the node, which then forwards to nodePort 32080 and NATs to pod:8080. That should work generally, but our health check is configured to use the service port name `http` -> the LB health check uses the port number 443. If the pod expects TLS handshake (443) but pod is plaintext 8080, the check will fail.

leo: exactly — we had this with the ssl passthrough experiment. If the ALB terminates TLS you'd set port 443 and targetPort 8080, but with NLB passthrough the LB expects the backend to speak TLS on the node (or raw TCP if configured).

marta: ok the gateway pods are plain HTTP (no TLS). we intended to let the LB handle TLS termination, but the infra owner switched to NLB passthrough instead of ALB. so mismatch.

irene: two quick fixes:
- switch back to ALB (HTTP/HTTPS) and keep service.port 443 -> targetPort 8080 but enable LB TLS termination; or
- keep NLB passthrough but change targetPort to 8443 and make pods serve TLS, or change service.port back to 8080 and let annotations handle TLS on LB.

samir: additionally check healthcheck protocol/port annotation: we have `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol` and `...-healthcheck-port`. If those are unset, the controller might use `port` value (443) which is wrong for plaintext pods.

marta: found annotations in TF: we were setting `aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: tls` and no explicit `healthcheck-port`. controller defaulted to port 443.

leo: minor gotcha — if you use named port (name: http) and your targetPort is numeric, controller sometimes uses the name to pick probe config; but with NodePort mode and `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` there's more nuance about where healthchecks land. Are you using Local?

marta: yes `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` (we set it to preserve client IP).

irene: then the NLB will target node IPs only if there are ready pods on that node. Healthcheck hits node IP:443 -> kube-proxy -> pod:8080 only on nodes with pods. If the pod doesn't speak TLS you'll see failing healthchecks and eventual 502s.

samir: proposed quick remediation: revert service.port to 8080 in TF, keep type NodePort, set LB annotations to `target-protocol: http` (or set backend-protocol: http) and set `healthcheck-port: 8080` — effectively tell the NLB to check plaintext 8080. That avoids changing pod stack.

marta: I can open a rollback PR. Should we also add a note to the ingress/gateway README about expected TLS termination modes?

leo: yes please. Add a checklist: (ALB vs NLB) termination mode, service.port vs targetPort mapping, healthcheck-port annotation, externalTrafficPolicy. Would've saved us today. :facepalm:

marta: opening PR now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/PR-3460 — rolls back port to 8080 and sets `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port: "8080"` and `...-backend-protocol: http`.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/terraform/PR-3460 plan looks clean.

irene: once PR merges monitor canary for 10m. If green we'll roll to prod.

samir: also pinging @netops — we might want a small postmortem note in runbook about this exact mismatch.

marta: thanks all. will add runbook blurb and the README note in the PR.

leo: :thumbsup:

marta: fwiw, adding unit test in TF module to catch inconsistent `backend-protocol` vs `target_port` would be great long-term. filing a follow-up issue.
